headline: 9 contracts catalogued across Plasma (primary) and Ethereum (partial); 2 core token proxies + 3 implementation addresses on Plasma, 2 Ethereum product addresses unresolvable from available evidence; GitHub repo is private.

findings.text: D1: Plasmascan name-tag search surfaced yzUSD token proxy (0x6695c0f8706c5ace3bdf8995073179cca47926dc) and syzUSD token proxy (0xc8a8df9b210243c55d31c73090f06787ad0a1bf6) on Plasma chain. Etherscan search for 'Yuzu Money' returned only unrelated memecoins; no Ethereum main-protocol contracts surfaced via name-tag. Ethereum product vault addresses (yzSyrup, yzCash) visible in dashboard as abbreviated 0xc985…09b1 and 0x224e…098d but full addresses not confirmed in fetched evidence.

D2: No dedicated deployed-contracts documentation page found at app.yuzu.money/docs or gitbook. The gitbook audits page lists audit reports but no canonical address registry. Transparency page (app.yuzu.money/transparency) provides proof-of-reserves UI but no contract address list. protocol_metadata.deployed_contracts_doc set to null.

D3: Five audits identified from gitbook: (1) Pashov Aug 2025, (2) Dedaub Oct 2025, (3) Pashov Jan 2026, (4) Dedaub Feb 2026 (PSM), (5) Pashov Jul 2026. Dedaub Oct 2025 audit references private repo github.com/Telos-Consilium/ouroboros-contracts at commit e72487426a8988d52acaa3a86b45000a5e82b13a; contract scope includes YuzuUSD, StakedYuzuUSD (ERC4626 vault), YuzuILP (Insurance Liquidity Pool), YuzuProto (base contract), and an unaudited treasury contract. Dedaub Feb 2026 PSM audit snippet references Plasma::0xb14e7d488371d22d39aff1b0c0f07ed2b532160f as StakedYuzuUSD prior implementation.

D4: protocol.github is null; no official GitHub org/repo recorded in per-protocol context. Dedaub audit reveals private repo github.com/Telos-Consilium/ouroboros-contracts — not publicly accessible; no broadcast artifacts fetchable. No deployment JSON, addresses.json, or README table found.

D5: Plasma chain: yzUSD proxy and syzUSD proxy confirmed. Ethereum chain: yzSyrup and yzCash vaults visible in dashboard but full addresses not recoverable from fetched evidence — recorded in unknowns[]. Monad chain: Monad mainnet not yet live as of analysis date; zero addresses surfaced from any source for Monad.
D6: No factory contracts identified in scope. YuzuILP (Insurance Liquidity Pool) and YuzuProto are base/singleton contracts, not factories. No enumeration attempted.

D7: Role taxonomy applied: yzUSD proxy = token; syzUSD proxy = vault/token; YuzuUSDV2 impl = other (implementation); StakedYuzuUSDV2 impl = other (implementation); prior StakedYuzuUSD impl = other (audit-era implementation). Treasury contract referenced in audits but address unknown.

D8: All addresses in admin_addresses[] trace to plasmascan.to search results (yzUSD, syzUSD proxies and impls) or Dedaub PSM audit snippet (0xb14e7d488371d22d39aff1b0c0f07ed2b532160f). Abbreviated Ethereum addresses (0xc985…09b1, 0x224e…098d) not included in admin_addresses[] — placed in unknowns[].

rationale.verdict: Discovery run walked protocol website, gitbook audits page, transparency page, two audit reports (Dedaub Oct 2025 full body, Pashov Aug 2025 metadata only), and Plasmascan search results. 5 Plasma-chain addresses confirmed from on-chain explorers; 2 Ethereum product vault addresses partially visible but unresolvable; treasury address unknown; Monad zero results. GitHub repo is private (Telos-Consilium/ouroboros-contracts). grade=unknown because no canonical deployed-contracts doc was found and several key addresses (Ethereum vaults, treasury, YuzuILP proxy, admin/owner addresses) remain unrecovered.

evidence.shows: Protocol dashboard listing products: Alpha (syzUSD senior tranche, yzPP junior), Prime (RWA), Marketplace (yzSyrup on Ethereum powered by Morpho/Euler/Fluid with address fragment 0xc985...09b1, yzCash on Ethereum powered by Curvance with address fragment 0x224e...098d). Confirms Ethereum deployment of vault products.
Five audits listed: Pashov Aug 2025, Dedaub Oct 2025, Pashov Jan 2026, Dedaub Feb 2026 (PSM), Pashov Jul 2026. Links to all audit PDFs/pages.

Dedaub Oct 2025 audit of YuzuUSD ecosystem. Confirms private repo https://github.com/Telos-Consilium/ouroboros-contracts at commit e72487426a8988d52acaa3a86b45000a5e82b13a. Contracts in scope: YuzuUSD, StakedYuzuUSD (ERC4626), YuzuILP (Insurance Liquidity Pool), YuzuProto (base). Treasury contract explicitly out of scope. Centralisation findings: admin controls poolSize (YuzuILP NAV), treasury address, supply cap, redemption fees. Protocol is upgradeable by design.
Proof-of-reserves page. Mentions Accountable, Hypernative, Fordefi, Chainlink as verification/monitoring partners. No contract addresses listed.

Plasmascan contract page for yzUSD (Yuzu USD token). Identified as EIP-1967 Transparent Proxy. Current implementation: YuzuUSDV2 at 0x32d7d5bf842d6ae28c9dd4fac4c6662cf9bf5cfe. Previous implementation: 0x90b1bc26e1ac873fc5043a9f658443daab674d85 (YuzuUSD). Supply ~44.65M yzUSD. Confirms upgradeable proxy pattern on Plasma chain.

Plasmascan token page for syzUSD (Staked Yuzu USD, ERC-4626 vault). Identified as EIP-1967 Transparent Proxy at 0xc8a8df9b210243c55d31c73090f06787ad0a1bf6. Current implementation: StakedYuzuUSDV2 at 0x926b292f3b0fa2af6e6561c2bca28f0625130ec8. Previous implementation: 0xb14e7d488371d22d39aff1b0c0f07ed2b532160f (StakedYuzuUSD). Supply ~46.1M syzUSD.

Dedaub Feb 2026 PSM audit snippet references Plasma::0xb14e7d488371d22d39aff1b0c0f07ed2b532160f as the StakedYuzuUSD implementation contract (prior to upgrade to StakedYuzuUSDV2), confirming it as an audit-era implementation address on Plasma chain.
GitHub page for Pashov Aug 2025 YuzuUSD security review PDF. Confirms Pashov audited YuzuUSD protocol. PDF not renderable; no contract addresses extractable from this fetch.

protocol_metadata.about: Yuzu Money is a DeFi yield protocol that issues yzUSD, a USDC-backed stablecoin, and wraps it in an ERC-4626 vault (syzUSD) that distributes yield to stakers. The protocol also offers an Insurance Liquidity Pool (YuzuILP) where USDC liquidity providers earn yield, and marketplace products (yzSyrup, yzCash) that deploy capital into third-party lending protocols on Ethereum. The system is centralized by design: an admin controls key parameters including the ILP's net asset value, treasury address, supply caps, and redemption fees, with collateral held off-chain in a treasury contract. Deployed primarily on Plasma chain, with Ethereum marketplace vaults and Monad deployment planned.
